# `pi_output_set`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set one or more auxiliary outputs (GPIO, PWM, DSLR, beeper) by name.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xf8250, GPIOController::WriteByIndex @0x324650, Write @0x323ab0 (64-bit build) |

Applies each named member in request order. Writes are sequential and not transactional: earlier writes persist when a later member fails. A success reply does not prove that every write took effect: the handler ignores the hardware-write return for dslr, esp and beep members. Failure paths that break out of the member loop after appending an error can also append the success members, so a reply can carry both error and result (duplicate envelope keys); treat the first code as authoritative and do not infer success from a trailing code 0. Numeric names without any digit in a port or gpio name are silently ignored.

Side effects: Changes output level or PWM duty, writes per-port setting name/state/value/is_pwm and the shared output cache; hardware effect is controlled by per-port flags. No rollback, no timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"pi_output_set"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Output settings keyed by name. Two spellings: a single object, or an array whose first element is that object. Each member name selects an output by case-sensitive substring, tested in this order: port, dslr, esp, beep, gpio. port<N> and gpio<N> take the first run of decimal digits in the name as N (port: zero-based port index; gpio: raw driver pin number, no handler bounds). Unrecognised names are ignored when their value type is acceptable. A boolean value means digital state at value 100. A numeric value means PWM percent with state true when the value exceeds 0.001. dslr and esp accept boolean, integer or real but always use digital mode at value 100 and compute state from the raw 32-bit value (any nonzero bit pattern, including integer -1 and negative zero, is true). beep always uses PWM mode; a boolean beep value leaves the value at 100, so beep:false still requests PWM 100 rather than clearing the output. An empty object succeeds and does nothing. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent, null or not an object (or array with no object first element) | `expected object param` |
| 209 | A member value is not a boolean, integer or real | `invalid value` |
| 207 | Unexpected regular-expression match shape while extracting the port/gpio number | `fail to operate` |
| 204 | Port index out of range, or computed PWM duty out of range | `out of limit` |
| 273 | GPIO connection or driver failure on a checked write | `GPIO operation failed` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, set-port - Turn port 1 on at 60 percent PWM and the DSLR line off (values invented):

```json
{"id":5,"method":"pi_output_set","params":{"port1":60,"dslr":false}}
```

Request, array-form - Array spelling with a boolean state:

```json
{"id":6,"method":"pi_output_set","params":[{"port0":true}]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_output_set","result":0,"code":0,"id":5}
```

Reply, wrong-type:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_output_set","error":"invalid value","code":209,"id":7}
```
